headline: The cost of insuring SpaceX's debt hit a record high as the company seeks $40 billion for AI chips.
score_reason: Specific market data from one outlet, with the $40 billion deal still in talks; pool score 7 kept.
importance_line: Lenders and bondholders are the first affected, though the $40 billion borrowing is still in talks and a single day's move in a risk gauge may not last.
summary: Seoul Economic Daily reports, citing ICE Data Services, that the cost of insuring SpaceX's debt against default hit an all-time high as SpaceX seeks about $40 billion from banks and investors to buy Nvidia's Vera Rubin AI computing platform, a plan the Financial Times reported on 6 Oct 2026. The extra interest investors demand on its bonds due 2036 rose to 193 basis points, from 140 when they were sold in June (a basis point is one hundredth of a percentage point), a sign that worry about the borrowing is spreading to the bond market.
